VICE-PRESIDENT (VP) OF INDIA

(Article 63-71)

Article 63: There shall be a Vice-President of India.

Article 64: Vice President shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

VP holds second highest constitutional post.
VP can act as President only for a maximum period of 6 months.

Article 65: Vice-President to act as President.

In the absence of the President:

  • Vice President performs functions as an Acting President.

Article 66: Election of Vice-President.

1) Elected by Electoral College:

  • All members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha)
  • Includes nominated members also.

2) Method of Election:

  • Proportional Representation + Single Transferable Vote (STV)
  • 20 proposers + 20 electors as seconders
  • Secret ballot voting
  • Required Security deposit: ₹15,000/-
  • Each voter has multiple preferences of voting.

3) Eligibility criteria:

  • must be a citizen of India
  • Must be of 35 years or more
  • Qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.

4) He shall not be a member of either house of the parliament and/or State Legislature (Same as President)

Article 67: Term of Office of Vice-President.

  • Can hold office upto 5 years.
  • Can resign to the President (and vice-versa)

Removal if:

  • Resolution initiated (only in Rajya Sabha)
  • Passed by effective majority in RS and simple majority in LS.
  • 14 days prior notice required.
  • Will continue in office until successor takes charge.

Article 68: Time of holding election to fill vacancy.

  • Vacancy caused due to expiration of the term of office of VP shall be completed before the expiration of the term.
  • If vacancy arises due to resignation, removal by Parliament, or death, then — Election must be held as soon as possible.

Article 69: Oath or affirmation by Vice-President.

  • Administered by the President or any person appointed on behalf of him.

Article 70: Discharge of President's functions in other contingencies.

Parliament may make provisions for the discharge of the President's functions in any contingency.

Article 71: Matters relating to election of President and Vice-President.

1) All doubts and disputes related to elections are handled by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final

2) If election is declared void by the SC, then the acts done by VP / President before the date of declaration are considered valid.

3) Parliament may regulate matters related to election of P/VP.

4) Election cannot be challenged on the ground that electoral college electing that person was incomplete.

Longest serving VP: M. Hamid Ansari (2007-2017).
He is the only VP to serve under 3 Presidents.

Article 72: Pardoning power of the President

Types of Pardoning Power of President:

1) Pardon — Completely removes punishment and conviction.

2) Commutation — changes the form of punishment.

3) Remission — Reduce the punishment period.

4) Respite — Lessen the punishment due to special conditions. (e.g., pregnancy)

5) Reprieve — Stay on execution for a temporary duration.

Q. What is the difference between the pardoning power of President and Governor?

Ans: The President can pardon death sentences and court-martial punishments while the Governor cannot. (Pardoning power of Governor is given in Article 161)

Kehar Singh vs Union of India Case (1988):

Pardoning power of the President is not subject to judicial review, unless the decision is arbitrary, mala fide, irrational, or discriminatory.

Judicial Powers of the President

  • Appoints Chief Justice and judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
  • Can seek advice from Supreme Court on any law or fact. However, the advice tendered by the SC is not binding on him.
  • Exercises pardoning powers as mentioned above.
